newsitem.title: USA: Miami hires New York firm Hawkins Delafield & Wood.
newsitem.headline: Miami hires New York firm Hawkins Delafield & Wood.

text.p: Miami has hired the New York law firm Hawkins Delafield & Wood, which specializes in municipal finance, to aid the city through its financial crisis.
Firm partner Richard Sigal declined to specify exactly what the firm's role would be but said it would draw on its experience in "bond disclosure and tax counsel matters."
"There's no contemplation, because of the oversignt board's being involved, that there will be any bankruptcy work here," Sigal told Reuters in a phone interview Thursday.
City commissioners voted last week to hire the firm to work with Miami law firm Holtzman, Krinzman, Equels & Furia, which was already advising the city.

Miami officials have confirmed that the Securities and Exchange Commission is looking into several Miami bond issues, but the federal regulators would not say whether the probe focuses on the city's failure to disclose to bondholders that its finances had deteriorated.

After several top officials resigned to face federal corruption charges, the city revealed that it had a $68 million deficit for the year that began Oct 1. Gov. Lawton Chiles declared a fiscal emergency and appointed an advisery board to oversee the recovery.
The board was scheduled to meet Jan 6 to begin reviewing the revised budget plan commissioners approved on Monday to close the budget gap. The board has until Jan 20 to accept or reject it.

Hawkins Delafield & Wood worked with the Municipal Assistance Corp during New York's fiscal crisis. Its clients include the New York cities of Buffalo, Yonkers and Troy, as well as cities in California and Connecticut.
"We've worked in a lot of these distress situations," Sigal said.
